cells.name: iptables, callers learn that a zone is lost: endpoints only

prediction.text: The algebra predicts a false removal: the replica can serve, but it leaves the EndpointSlice and the rules of each node. The band is 39.6 s to 55.355 s after the fault. The node of the target is lost for the hold (70 s). Each packet on its link drops, and its kubelet is frozen. Its lease expires, thus the node lifecycle controller marks the target not ready, and it leaves the rules 39.6 s–55.355 s after the fault. No client is in the lost zone. Each connection on the target fails one request at its timeout (2 s). Then a new connection picks a backend, one turn (0.16 s) later. Each pick goes to the target at random, thus the failures of the 16 connections are negative binomial: 6–28 in 95 % of the runs. A chain longer than 13 picks has a chance of 0.001 at the most. The last pick of a chain comes 3.92 s after the fault at the latest, before the removal. Thus the removal changes nothing.

cells.why: Each of the 3 counted runs agrees with the prediction. The median is 50.393 s. The counted runs measured 46.025 s to 51.048 s.

cells.name: iptables, callers learn that a zone is lost: in band on HTTP/2 (GOAWAY)

prediction.text: The algebra predicts a false removal: the replica can serve, but it leaves the EndpointSlice and the rules of each node. The band is 39.6 s to 55.355 s after the fault. The node of the target is lost for the hold (70 s). Each packet on its link drops, and its kubelet is frozen. Its lease expires, thus the node lifecycle controller marks the target not ready, and it leaves the rules 39.6 s–55.355 s after the fault. No client is in the lost zone. The established flow keeps the session of a client on the target after the removal. Each stream on it fails at its timeout (2 s). TCP retransmits with a backoff, and firing 9 of the timer is the first after the heal: 102.681 s–108.78 s after the fault. Then the target resets the session, or it sends GOAWAY, and the client opens a new session. If the target had no unacked data, its GOAWAY at the thaw ends the failures near the heal. Thus the last failure starts 67.98 s after the fault at the earliest. 0–2 of the 2 sessions are on the target, thus about 0–10878 requests fail.

cells.why: Each of the 3 counted runs agrees with the prediction. The median is 49.002 s. The counted runs measured 42.4 s to 51.553 s.

cells.name: iptables, callers learn that a zone is lost: in band on HTTP/2 with a session check

prediction.text: The algebra predicts a false removal: the replica can serve, but it leaves the EndpointSlice and the rules of each node. The band is 39.6 s to 55.355 s after the fault. The node of the target is lost for the hold (70 s). Each packet on its link drops, and its kubelet is frozen. Its lease expires, thus the node lifecycle controller marks the target not ready, and it leaves the rules 39.6 s–55.355 s after the fault. No client is in the lost zone. The client checks its session: a PING after 0.5 s with no frame, and a close with no ACK in 0.5 s. The first session on the target closes 0.98 s–1.5 s after the fault, before its first stream timeout (2 s). Each stream on it fails at the close, 49–76 streams. The next request opens a new session. cells.why: Each of the 3 counted runs agrees with the prediction. The median is 50.695 s. The counted runs measured 47.14 s to 50.819 s.
